subject: stm32/usart: fix error msg for lptim
label: not_a_fix
evidence: The commit message is 'stm32/usart: fix error msg for lptim', and the only hunk changes the last argument of the trace! call 'Using {} oversampling, desired baudrate: {}, actual baudrate: {}' from 'pclk_freq.0 / div' to '(pclk_freq.0 * mul as u32) / div'; no register write, return value or control flow changes, only the printed 'actual baudrate' for the LPUART case where mul is 256. This is a log-text change, which counts as printing, not a behavioural fix. For completeness, py32-hal's configure in src/usart/mod.rs prints the same message with 'kernel_clock.0 / brr * mul', which already includes mul, and mul is always 1 there because the only kind is Kind::Uart. py32-hal's trace! macro only forwards its arguments to log/defmt, so even a wrong value there would not change runtime behaviour.

subject: stm32: Fix half-duplex uart reconfigure
label: same_bug
evidence: The embassy commit 'stm32: Fix half-duplex uart reconfigure' explains that the duplex config field 'is private and defaults to Full, so a user-supplied Config passed to set_config/reconfigure cannot express half-duplex', and changes configure to use 'config.duplex.is_half() || r.cr3().read().hdsel()' for both the HDSEL write and the TE/RE choice. py32-hal's configure in src/usart/mod.rs is the same logic before the fix: it writes 'w.set_hdsel(config.half_duplex)' and branches on 'if config.half_duplex', where half_duplex is a private field (commented 'private: set by new_half_duplex, not by the user.') that defaults to false and is only set to true on the by-value copy inside new_half_duplex and new_blocking_half_duplex. Every public set_config (Uart via SetConfig, UartTx, UartRx) calls reconfigure, which calls configure(info, kernel_clock, config, cr.re(), cr.te()) with the user's Config, so HDSEL is cleared and TE/RE are set as for full-duplex. Nothing else in py32-hal preserves HDSEL, and the fix needs only reading CR3.HDSEL, which py32-hal already does in its read and write paths, so there is no hardware or feature reason for it not to apply.

evidence_refs.quote: // private: set by new_half_duplex, not by the user.

title: Calling set_config on a half-duplex UART in py32-hal clears the half-duplex bit and silently switches it back to full-duplex.
summary: embassy-stm32 fixed this on 2026-06-02 (commit 013fc0d) by making configure keep half-duplex mode when the HDSEL bit is already set, because users cannot set the private duplex field in a Config they pass to set_config. py32-hal's configure still takes half-duplex mode only from its private half_duplex field, which is false in any Config a user can build, and writes it straight into HDSEL. So changing, for example, the baud rate of a UART created with new_half_duplex or new_blocking_half_duplex clears HDSEL and enables TE/RE as for full-duplex. The read and write paths only switch direction when HDSEL is set, so the single-wire link stops working as half-duplex without any error. The embassy patch can be carried over with only the field name changed.

subject: nrf/gpio: fix missing setting input as disconnected.
label: not_needed_hw
evidence: The commit 'nrf/gpio: fix missing setting input as disconnected.' is a real fix for nRF: writing PIN_CNF with all-zero fields left the input buffer connected, so set_as_disconnected and deconfigure_pin now write the INPUT field as Disconnect through conf(), which returns the nRF per-pin PinCnf register. py32-hal's src/gpio.rs is 'modified from embassy-stm32' and has no PinCnf register or INPUT field: its pins are configured through MODER/PUPDR/OTYPER/OSPEEDR, and SealedPin::set_as_disconnected simply calls set_as_analog, which writes Moder::ANALOG. Of the three hunks, the Drop change is already the form py32-hal uses (Flex::drop calls self.pin.set_as_disconnected()), the set_as_disconnected change depends on the nRF-only INPUT field, and deconfigure_pin has no counterpart because py32-hal has no PSEL concept (no psel, deconfigure_pin or PinCnf anywhere in src/). The register the fix depends on is absent on the other side.

subject: stm32/dma: fix BDMA mem to mem
label: not_needed_absent
evidence: The commit 'stm32/dma: fix BDMA mem to mem' adds one line to the BDMA branch of configure, 'w.set_mem2mem(dir == Dir::MemoryToMemory);', so that transfers with embassy's Dir::MemoryToMemory direction set the channel's MEM2MEM bit. py32-hal's DMA driver has no memory-to-memory direction at all: its Dir enum in src/dma/mod.rs has only MemoryToPeripheral and PeripheralToMemory, and the From<Dir> mapping in src/dma/dma.rs covers just those two. Every caller of configure (Transfer::new_read_raw, new_write_raw, new_write_repeated and the two ring-buffer constructors) passes one of those two directions, and configure always writes the channel CR with set_dir(dir.into()) and set_pinc(false), so a memory-to-memory transfer cannot be requested. Since the direction the fix keys on does not exist on the py32-hal side, there is nothing to fix.

subject: dma: add write_mem2mem methods for fixed-dest m2m
label: not_a_fix
evidence: The commit message is 'dma: add write_mem2mem methods for fixed-dest m2m' and says it 'Added write_mem2mem and write_mem2mem_raw to explicitly support memory-to-memory DMA transfers where the destination address is fixed', which is a new API. The second hunk only adds those two new public methods. The first hunk adds the arm '(Increment::Memory, Dir::MemoryToMemory) => (Incmode::Increment, Incmode::Fixed)' in the MDMA branch of configure; in the parent commit no caller passed that combination (the only MemoryToMemory caller, transfer_raw, passes Increment::Both, which the earlier '(Increment::Both, _)' arm matches, and every other caller uses PeripheralToMemory or MemoryToPeripheral), so the arm serves only the new write_mem2mem_raw and changes no existing behaviour. Both hunks are therefore part of a new feature, not a fix. For reference, py32-hal's DMA has neither MDMA nor a memory-to-memory direction: its Dir enum has only MemoryToPeripheral and PeripheralToMemory, DmaInfo has only the Dma variant, and configure takes a plain 'incr_mem: bool'.

subject: chore: fix build
label: not_needed_absent
evidence: The commit ('chore: fix build') only respells stm32-metapac enum variants in embassy-stm32/src/gpio.rs (all 9 hunks: Ot::PUSHPULL to PUSH_PULL, CnfOut::OPENDRAIN to OPEN_DRAIN, Pupdr::PULLUP to PULL_UP, Ospeedr::LOWSPEED to LOW_SPEED and so on), right after its parent commit 96819805e moved embassy-stm32/Cargo.toml to a new stm32-metapac tag; which variant each line writes does not change. Under the build-fix rule the question is whether embassy-nrf would also stop building after that PAC bump, and it would not: embassy-nrf depends on nrf-pac, not stm32-metapac, and its gpio.rs takes its register values from crate::pac::gpio::vals of nrf-pac. The nRF Flex functions with the same names (set_as_input, set_as_output, set_as_input_output) write a single per-pin conf() register with nrf-pac values such as vals::Dir::Input and vals::Pull::Pullup, and embassy-nrf/src/gpio.rs never references Ot, CnfOut, Pupdr or Ospeedr. So the code this commit had to rename does not exist on the nRF side.

subject: fix: fix incorrect logic for buffered usart transmission complete.
label: not_needed_absent
evidence: The STM32 fix makes the buffered USART interrupt treat the TC (transmission complete) status bit as an event only when TCIE is enabled, which the driver arms just for the last byte; without the check, any interrupt entry that found TC set ran the completion path (clear TCIE, re-enable the receiver, set tx_done and wake flush). hpm-hal's on_interrupt in src/uart/buffered.rs has no transmission-complete path at all: it reads LSR, and its only TX branch is 'if lsr.thre()', which sends the next byte from the ring buffer or, when the buffer is empty, clears ETHEI and sets tx_done. There is no TC-like flag and no completion-interrupt enable to gate; write() starts a transfer by writing the first byte to THR itself instead of pending the interrupt, and flush() only waits for that buffer-empty report, so the fixed logic has no counterpart here. Separately, and not part of this hunk, write() clears tx_done (line 427) before committing the new bytes (line 440) outside a critical section, a window the STM32 driver closes with commit_tx.

title: The STM32C0 SPI driver likely reads the wrong address when receiving and writes the data register at full width, which stm32g0xx-hal fixed by moving both accesses to the 8-bit dr8() register.
summary: stm32g0xx-hal moved its SPI byte read and write onto the 8-bit dr8() data register on 2024-12-19 (this commit, following 'fix SPI transfer' the same day), and did so again in 865ed9d after a merge had brought the old lines back. stm32c0xx-hal still has the code from before both fixes: read() does ptr::read_volatile(&self.spi.dr() as *const _ as *const u8), which reads the temporary reference returned by dr() instead of the register, and send() writes the data register at full width. If this is not fixed, read(), and the blocking transfer and write that call it, most likely return a constant byte instead of the received data, and send() keeps the full-width write that G0 replaced with a byte-wide one. The change has to be adapted to C0's embedded-hal 0.2 read/send, and the repository does not show whether the stm32c0 0.16 PAC provides dr8(); if it does not, a byte pointer taken from the register address is needed.
